text:
support_jess: FYI customer acme-inc on Hosted API is seeing intermittent 401s today after they rotated their IdP keys ~09:10 UTC. Error from our side is "invalid_signature". They say it affects ~10% of requests.

support_jess: sample log snippet from our gateway: 
```
[09:11:02] validate_token: token=kid=ephemeral-2026-03-17 -> result=OK
[09:11:04] validate_token: token=kid=ephemeral-2026-03-17 -> result=invalid_signature
[09:11:05] jwks_fetch: cache_hit age=120s ETag="abc123" status=304
[09:11:06] validate_token: token=kid=ephemeral-2026-03-17 -> result=invalid_signature
```

support_jess: their token header looks like: 
```
{"alg":"RS256","kid":"ephemeral-2026-03-17"}
```

omar: do we know whether the IdP published the new key to JWKS immediately? can we see the jwks.json response headers they get?

support_jess: they pasted their fetch of jwks.json (from IdP edge): 
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Cache-Control: public, max-age=300
ETag: "abc123"
Content-Type: application/json

{"keys":[{"kty":"RSA","kid":"ephemeral-2026-03-17","n":"...","e":"AQAB"}]}
```

support_jess: they also showed a later fetch that returned the older key set (no ephemeral kid) due to CDN caching on their side. but our logs show we got 304 (If-None-Match) and kept the cached keys.

maya: this smells like a race between rotation and JWKS caching. two common modes: (A) token signed with *new* key but our cache doesn't have it yet -> kid-not-found or invalid_signature; (B) token signed with old key but IdP removed it too fast. here it looks like new ephemeral kid is present in origin but some fetches see an older cached JWKS and our cache honors 304.

kevin: on kid-miss we should already be trying to re-fetch ignoring cache TTL. do we have that code path? iirc we do a conditional GET with If-None-Match and if 304 we keep old keys. that fails if the origin rotated keys and the CDN returned 304 incorrectly for a very short interval (race).

omar: can we get a repro? steps i recommend for engineering:
1) request token from IdP before rotation -> signed by old-kid
2) call our API (works)
3) trigger rotation on IdP -> origin now serves new jwks.json with ephemeral kid but CDN edge may still return previous response and/or 304 to conditional GETs
4) request token from IdP signed by new ephemeral kid -> some of our validation attempts will 401 until our server fetches the new key (or cache expires)

omar: repro curl sequence (can run against their staging IdP):
```
# get token (new ephemeral key after rotation)
TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST https://idp.acme/.well-known/token -d '...' | jq -r .access_token)
# validate against our API
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.example/v1/ping
# inspect gateway logs -> should show invalid_signature
# force jwks refetch from our service (temp) by hitting admin endpoint or restarting instance
curl -i https://api.redwood.example/_admin/force-jwks-refresh
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.example/v1/ping # should succeed
```

triage-bot: Observed pattern: 401 spike correlated with 09:10-09:18 window across 3 hosts. JWKS conditional fetches returned 304 in that window.

maya: short-term mitigation options:
- instruct customer to use longer-lived intermediary keys (not ephemeral) during rolling rotation (not ideal)
- server-side: on kid-miss OR signature failure, immediately do an unconditional JWKS GET (bypass If-None-Match) and revalidate once. also consider a small backoff loop (2 attempts).
- alternative: keep previous JWKS snapshot for X seconds after a rotation event detected (i.e., prefer union of last N snapshots).

kevin: technical impl notes: our current cache uses ETag + max-age and avoids unconditional fetches to reduce IdP load. change: when validate() gets kid-not-found OR invalid_signature and the kid is not in current set, we should invalidate local cache and fetch origin with Cache-Control: no-cache or append ?_ts= to bypass CDN. fallback: accept 2xx from origin and update cache. also add metrics: jwks_refetch_on_kid_miss_count, jwks_unexpected_304_count.

omar: agree. small feature flagged hotfix: "jwks-refetch-on-kid-miss" default off. implement in runtime + unit tests. add e2e scenario in infra tests that simulates 304 from CDN and ensures one refetch succeeds.

kevin: i'll own the runtime PR and can do a quick canary to dedicated pool. estimated: PR today, canary tomorrow, full rollout if metrics look good.

support_jess: i'll send a short support note to acme with repro steps and ask them to keep an eye for 401s and timestamped logs. will propose they temporarily increase JWKS TTL at origin or add stale-while-revalidate header if their CDN supports it.

omar: follow-ups: (1) add observability alert for sudden increase in invalid_signature with accompanying jwks_conditional_304 spike, (2) add internal runbook step to force jwks refresh on 401 bursts, (3) postmortem if we see customer impact > 5min.

support_jess: thanks all. assigning follow-ups: @kevin -> runtime PR + canary, @omar -> test harness + e2e, @maya -> alert/dashboard tweak, @support_jess -> customer comms. :thumbsup:
